newsitem.title: USA: Dlr pares overseas losses, ends higher vs mark,yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr pares overseas losses, ends higher vs mark,yen.

text.p: The dollar closed higher against the mark and the yen on Monday as investors spied a buying opportunity after weakness in overseas trading.

In a fit of election jitters before U.S. trade began, investors flocked to the mark at the expense of sterling and other European currencies on news that British Prime Minister John Major was calling a general election on May 1.

The prospect of political uncertainty in Britain, where Major's incumbent Conservative party lags the opposing Labor party by more than 20 points in opinion polls, prompted a sell-off in the British pound.

Lingering uncertainties about the timetable for European monetary union also helped buoy the mark overseas, pushing it higher against other European currencies and the Japanese yen, and ultimately filtering through to a weaker dollar.
"The dollar was trading a little heavy today at the start, but we had a nice bounce mostly on short-covering," said Marc Chandler, senior currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The dollar closed at 1.6917/22 against the mark, up from its opening Monday at 1.6865/70. The opening was substantially lower than the dollar's Friday close of 1.6945/55.
Against the yen, the dollar was modestly firmer, ending the day at 123.76/81 against 123.44/49 at the open.

Comments from German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, who said on Monday that strict adherence to criteria for the single currency was more important than meeting the 1999 timetable, also buoyed the mark.
"Waigel's comments, that meeting the criteria was more important than the timing, concerned the market," said Hillel Waxman, chief foreign exchange dealer at Bank Leumi Trust Co of New York.
Monday's strong mark gains prompted the Bank of Spain and the Bank of Italy to sell marks for lire and pesetas, respectively, in an effort to prop up their own currencies.
The dollar gained against the yen despite news that Japan's trade surpolus had risen 6.5 percent year-over-year in February to 686.72 billion yen.
"That says that underlying sentiment to the dollar was not all that negative or they would have seized on the (figures) to sell," Chandler said.
In other trade on Monday, the British pound slid to $1.5880/90 from its opening at $1.5910/15.

The dollar ended higher against the Swiss franc at 1.4600/10 compared to its opening of 1.4515/25 and higher against the Canadian dollar, climbing to C$1.3699/04 compared to its opening at C$1.3675/80. The Australian dollar closed at $0.7915/20 versus $0.7929/39 at the opening.
(( J. Westhoven, N. American Treasury Desk 212 859 1660))
